display.title: Episode 320: The Strange Gift (Pesach)
display.summary_short: A week before Pesach, Uncle Yossi teaches about the time of our freedom and the final Geulah, a young guest says the Shema, and a father tells the story of Nachum Ish Gamzu's box of sand.
display.summary_long: Broadcast a week and a half before Pesach 5748. Uncle Yossi explains 'Zman Cheiruseinu', the time of our freedom: every day we should see ourselves as if we ourselves left Mitzrayim, and remembering the miracles with real trust in Hashem brings them again in our own days. He reviews the Pesach preparations, selling the chametz and having shmurah matzah for the Seder nights, which the Zohar calls food of faith and food of healing, and speaks about the final Geulah that will end golus forever, with a saying of the Frierdiker Rebbe: not many salvations, but one lasting one. After the Hakochainik march, a young member of Tzivos Hashem recites the Shema and one of the Twelve Pesukim. Story time brings 'The Strange Gift': at bedtime a father tells his son how Nachum Ish Gamzu's gift of diamonds for the king was stolen and replaced with sand, and how, with the help of Eliyahu HaNavi, the sand became miraculous on the battlefield. The show ends with the Shabbos candle time and an invitation to the Pesach Experience on Chol HaMoed.
display.lesson: Everything Hashem does is for the good, even when we cannot see it yet: 'Gam zu l'tovah'.

advisories.note: A king forbids Torah study; Nachum Ish Gamzu is thrown into prison and threatened with death.
The thieving innkeeper is put to death by the king.
